Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Acute dysuria with mild suprapubic crampy pain for a few days; brief visible hematuria today; malodorous urine; no fever, flank/back pain, nausea/vomiting; no urinary frequency/urgency noted.
- Primary impression: Acute uncomplicated cystitis (acute lower UTI) — likely, consistent with transcript and DDx.
- Differential considerations (from DDx, consistent with history):
  - Urethritis due to STI (e.g., chlamydia/gonorrhea/Mycoplasma) — possible given new partner and no prior STI screen; absence of discharge lowers but does not exclude.
  - Vaginitis (BV or trichomonas) causing external dysuria — lower likelihood given no discharge/pruritus; malodor noted but source unclear.
- Allergy: Clindamycin — causes swelling (documented).
- Plan per clinician: Empiric antibiotics for presumed simple UTI: either nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim, 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days (exact agent and dose not documented). Increase oral fluids; may try cranberry juice. Avoid sexual activity until symptoms resolve; continue barrier contraception. Safety-net advice: return/seek care if fever, back pain, worsening systemic symptoms, or no improvement by end of week. Consider pregnancy test if any concern.

Management Plan
-  Empiric antibiotic therapy: Nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim prescribed for 3 days, 1 tablet twice daily; exact agent and dose not documented. Hydration encouraged; cranberry juice optional. Abstain from sex until symptoms clear; continue condom use thereafter. Return if not improved by end of week or earlier if fever, flank/back pain, or feeling more unwell. Consider pregnancy test if concerned about pregnancy.

Consider:
- Pathology tests as above:  Consider urinalysis and urine culture if symptoms persist/atypical, NAAT for chlamydia/gonorrhea (and Mycoplasma if available) given new partner/no prior screen, and urine pregnancy test.

- Acute uncomplicated cystitis — High likelihood. Short-duration dysuria, suprapubic discomfort, malodorous urine, and brief hematuria without fever/flank pain support lower UTI.
- Urethritis due to STI — Moderate likelihood. Sexually active with a relatively new partner, no prior STI screen, dysuria without frequency/urgency could fit; lack of discharge lowers probability.
- Vaginitis (BV/trichomonas) — Low to moderate likelihood. Malodor noted but no discharge/pruritus; hematuria favors urinary source.
